question:
Outbound email notifications show reversed direction
When our team sends an email to a customer through Front, the Zulip notification shows the email coming from the customer to us instead of going from us to the customer. The subject line and conversation link are correct, but the sender and recipient addresses are swapped compared to how inbound messages appear.

Inbound message direction is reversed
When a customer emails us and the message arrives in Zulip, the notification says it was sent from my team member to the customer, instead of from the customer to my team member. The from and to parties are swapped. Outbound messages show the same problem in reverse.

Unassigned notification omits who was unassigned
When a conversation is unassigned, the Zulip message only shows who performed the unassignment but not which team member was removed as the assignee. For example it says "Unassigned by Jane" without mentioning Bob, who was actually unassigned. I expected to see both people mentioned, similar to how the assignment notification shows both the assigner and the assignee.

Outbound reply notifications omit the subject line
When a teammate replies to a customer, the Zulip stream notification only shows who replied to whom, without including the conversation subject. Both new inbound and outbound message notifications include the subject, so I expected reply notifications to show it too.

Inbound message shows sender and recipient backwards
When I receive an inbound email from a customer through Front, the Zulip notification shows the direction reversed — it says the message came from our team to the customer instead of from the customer to our team. Outbound messages display correctly. I expected both directions to show who actually sent and received each message.

Notion updates never appear in Zulip after setup
I connected my Notion workspace to Zulip using the webhook integration. The initial verification succeeded and I received a message confirming the setup. However, after that, none of my Notion page or database changes ever show up in Zulip. I verified that my Notion webhook is correctly configured and sending events. I expected real-time updates from Notion to appear in Zulip just like other integrations do.

Verification token missing from setup message
When I add the Notion integration to a stream, the verification message appears but the token itself is blank. I can't complete the setup because I have nothing to paste into Notion's webhook configuration.

Application crashes on startup with an assertion error
When starting the application, the template loading system fails with an assertion error before any pages can render. The crash happens during initialization when the two-factor template engine tries to discover its template directories. I haven't changed any template settings from the defaults.

Two-factor authentication templates not found after upgrade
After upgrading, users are seeing template-not-found errors when the login page tries to render two-factor authentication forms. The main login works fine, but the OTP input section is broken. I haven't changed any settings.

Expected instead: The two-factor authentication templates should render correctly as they did before the upgrade.

Stream wildcard mentions in user group mentions are silently ignored
When I mention a user group using @*all* or @*stream*, the system does not treat it as a channel wildcard mention. Users subscribed to all channels do not get notified, even though they would be if I used @**all** instead. I expected any occurrence of the wildcard spelling to trigger notifications for everyone.

Mixed silent and non-silent group mentions don't respect order
When I mention a user group multiple times in one message using both silent and normal syntax, the notification behavior doesn't match what I'd expect from the last mention. If I first use normal mention syntax and then switch to silent for the same group, I still get notified. I expected the final mention type in the message to determine whether notifications are sent.

Cannot mention user whose full name matches a wildcard
When I try to mention a user named "topic" using @**topic**, they don't receive a notification. Instead, Zulip treats it as a topic-wide notification. The same issue affects users named "channel", "stream", "everyone", "all", or "topic".

Mentions of nested user groups don't notify members
When I mention a user group that is nested inside another group, the mention doesn't notify any members. Mentioning top-level groups works fine, but as soon as the group is a subgroup, nobody gets notified even though the mention appears in the message.

Mentioning a user group sometimes results in a server error
When I try to mention a user group in a message, the system sometimes throws an unexpected error instead of letting me send the message or telling me I'm not allowed to mention the group.

Plan name not displayed for community tier
When we try to view our account's plan details after switching to the community edition, the plan name doesn't appear and an error occurs. Other plan types show their names correctly.

Plan status shows an error when switching tiers immediately
When I change my team's plan tier to take effect right away, the plan page throws an error instead of showing the current status. The issue goes away once the switch completes. I expected the status text to display correctly for all plan states, including mid-change transitions.

License count crashes on billing page
When I visit the billing settings page to check our current license count, the page crashes with an error. This happens on our newly created organization account where we haven't added any team members yet. I expected to see zero displayed rather than a crash.

License count not shown when plan is downgrading
When my organization's plan is set to downgrade at the end of the billing cycle, the license count for the next renewal period is blank. I expected to see the reduced number of licenses so I could plan accordingly.

Cloud Community plan customers not receiving invoices
We purchased the Cloud Community plan for our organization and our account shows as active, but no invoice has ever been generated. Other paid plans are being billed correctly on schedule.

Attachment file size doesn't match actual content
When downloading an attachment on a local file storage setup, the Content-Length header sometimes doesn't match the actual data received. The download appears to stop early or the file seems corrupted. This happens intermittently, suggesting it depends on timing.

I expected the reported file size to always match what I actually receive when downloading.

Export progress indicator never updates
When I download a workspace export, the progress bar stays at 0% for the entire duration and then jumps to 100% when the file finishes copying. There's no intermediate feedback about how much of the export has been prepared.

Export tarballs remain on disk after deletion
When an admin deletes a realm's exported tarball, the operation completes without error but the file is never actually removed from storage. The tarball continues to occupy disk space even though the deletion appeared to succeed. I expected the export file to be fully cleaned up from the server.

Attachment replacement keeps old content
When I replace an uploaded message attachment with a new file, the old version stays visible instead of being updated with my replacement. I expected the new file to take over immediately.

Attachment thumbnails not cleaned up when deleting messages
When I delete a message that contained an image attachment, the main attachment file is removed but the thumbnail images are left behind on the server. Over time, this leads to wasted disk space from orphaned thumbnail files.

Desktop app version check seems broken
Even after updating my Zulip desktop app to a clearly newer version, I'm still getting warnings that my client is outdated. Other users on our server with the same updated version see the same false warnings. The version comparison appears to be producing incorrect results.

iPad users on newer iOS versions are not recognized as iOS devices. When I open the Zulip mobile app on my iPad running a recent version of iOS, the server doesn't detect that I'm on iOS and treats my client differently than iPhone users. On older iOS versions the same iPad worked fine. I expected all iPads to be identified as iOS just like iPhones.

Pronouns field missing on mobile after server upgrade
After our server was upgraded, my pronouns custom profile field disappeared from the mobile app. It still shows up fine in my web browser. I didn't change any settings—the field was there before the upgrade.

Desktop app flagged as outdated after update
After updating the Zulip desktop application to the newest release, my client is still flagged as outdated and I cannot send messages. I have restarted the app multiple times, but the block remains in place.

Realm admin sees server upgrade warning before regular users
After deploying a new server version, I (as the realm admin) immediately see the 'your server needs upgrading' warning banner, but regular users on the same server do not see it yet. The warning appears for admins right away while non-admins are given roughly a month of leeway. I expected everyone to see the same warning timeline regardless of their role.

Webhook fixtures sent in unpredictable order
When I use the bulk send feature for a webhook integration, the bot receives fixture events in a different order each time I run it. This makes debugging impossible when the sequence of events matters for the workflow I'm testing.

Expected: fixtures should always be sent in the same consistent order.

Fixture body parsing ignores file extensions
When I request fixtures for an integration, the body of each fixture is sometimes a parsed JSON object and sometimes a raw string, with no clear pattern. A text file whose contents happen to be valid JSON gets parsed into an object, while the endpoint should use the file extension to decide whether to parse or return raw content. I expected all bodies to consistently follow the file extension convention.

Webhook fixture messages arrive with the wrong Content-Type header
When I use the development panel to test a webhook integration, the Content-Type header on outgoing fixture requests does not always match the payload. A JSON body sometimes arrives as text/plain, causing my server to reject it. I expected the header to consistently reflect whether the message is JSON or plain text.

Inconsistent response format on non-200 webhook responses
When testing a webhook fixture, the response comes back as raw HTML or plain text whenever the webhook endpoint returns anything other than a 200 status code. I expected all responses to be consistently formatted as JSON so I can parse them the same way regardless of the status code.

Integration name lookup fails with different capitalization
When I try to load webhook fixtures using a different capitalization than the registered name—like "GitHub" instead of "github"—the system says the integration doesn't exist, even though it clearly does. I expected the lookup to accept any capitalization since the integration is available.

Included markdown loses its final blank line
When I include a markdown file that ends with a blank line, that blank line disappears in the rendered output. The last paragraph of the included content runs directly into whatever follows it in the parent document.

Included markdown files render as raw text
When I use an include statement to embed another markdown file, the content from that file shows up as unformatted text instead of being parsed by the markdown engine. Headers, lists, and other formatting from the included file appear literally rather than being rendered.

Include syntax ignored in quoted blocks
When I write an include macro inside a blockquote using tab indentation, the processor doesn't recognize it and renders the literal braces and exclamation marks instead of expanding the file. The same include works fine at the start of a line with no indentation.

Include statements show as literal text
When I use the include directive to embed reusable content into a message, the raw directive text appears in the rendered output instead of the embedded content. Other messages without the directive render correctly.

Include statements fail to find referenced files
When I use the include syntax in any documentation page, every attempt to pull in content from other markdown files fails with file-not-found errors, even though the referenced files exist at the expected paths relative to the documentation root. This happens across all sections of the docs, not just one area.

Email log accumulates duplicates on repeated runs
When I regenerate test emails, the log page keeps showing all previous emails plus the new ones instead of a clean set. I expected each generation to produce only the freshly generated batch.

Setting a forwarding address shows raw JSON instead of refreshing the page
When I enter an email forwarding address and submit the form on the development email log page, the browser displays a raw JSON response rather than reloading the page with my new address displayed. I expected the form submission to complete and the page to refresh showing the updated forwarding address.

Meeting creator joins as viewer when someone else clicks the link first
When I create a BigBlueButton video call and share the link with another admin, that person sometimes joins as the meeting host with full controls while I end up as a regular participant with limited permissions. This happens because the first person to click the join link gets moderator access, even if they didn't create the meeting. I expected the person who started the call to always be the moderator.

OAuth registration fails after authorizing video provider
After clicking "Connect Account" for a video call provider and completing the authorization on the provider's site, I'm redirected back to Zulip but the account linking fails instead of completing successfully.

Video call creation crashes with a server error when Zoom returns an unexpected response
When creating a video call, if the Zoom API returns an error response without the expected error code field (for example during an outage or with a non-JSON error page), the page crashes with a server error instead of showing a proper failure message. This makes it impossible to tell whether the issue is with Zoom's service or something else.
I expected the call creation to fail gracefully with a clear error message regardless of what format Zoom's error response comes in.

Disconnecting Zoom integration doesn't actually remove access
After disconnecting my Zoom integration, I can still create Zoom meetings through Zulip. The disconnect action appears to succeed, but my Zoom account remains linked and functional.

BigBlueButton meeting host parameter silently ignored
When I request a BigBlueButton meeting link through the API for a specific user, the designated host doesn't get moderator privileges. Instead, whoever makes the API request becomes the moderator. I expected the user I specified to have full moderator controls in the meeting.

Messages from public-history streams shown as read before viewing
When I join a stream that has public history enabled, old messages from before I joined appear as already read, even though I haven't opened them. I expected only messages I've actually viewed to be marked as read.

Bulk message send leaves some recipients without unread markers
When I send a message to a channel with many subscribers, a few of them never see the unread indicator on it. It only happens occasionally and seems to affect different people each time. I expected every recipient to get the message marked unread.

Read flag not appearing in message flags
When I mark messages as read, they continue to display as unread in my conversation view. Starred and other flags update correctly, but the read status never reflects until I fully reload the page.

Joining a stream leaves some historical messages missing from my view
After I subscribe to a stream with many old messages, several of them don't appear in my timeline even though I should have access to them. Other messages from the same stream show up fine right away. I expected all historical messages in that stream to become visible once I joined.

Expected behavior: All messages in the stream should be accessible after subscribing, not just a subset.

Users who sent exactly ten messages treated as idle after import
After importing data, some users who sent exactly ten messages are incorrectly classified as long-term idle, causing slower page loads on their first visit. The algorithm is supposed to consider anyone who sent ten or more messages as active.

Custom emoji import fails intermittently
When importing custom emojis from another platform, some emojis fail to appear even though the import process completes without errors. The missing emojis seem random across runs, and re-running the same import sometimes causes previously-missing emojis to appear correctly.

Wildcard mentions lost during Slack import
After importing from Slack, users who were mentioned with @all or @everyone don't see the mention notification on those messages. Regular @-mentions still work correctly, but the wildcard ones are silently dropped.

Imported files become publicly accessible
After importing from a platform with restricted file sharing, all uploaded files become accessible to every member of the organization. Files that were originally limited to specific conversations or channels are now visible to anyone who can view the associated messages.

Messages show attachment indicator even without attachments
After importing messages from another platform, every message displays an attachment icon, including plain text messages that clearly contain no files. Only messages with actual files should show this indicator.

Outgoing webhook bot stops responding after integration update
My bot that posts messages to an external service stopped responding to mentions after I updated its integration settings through the admin panel. The webhook queue shows the message was triggered but no request was ever sent. I expected the bot to continue processing mentions normally.

Bot service lookup crashes when two services share the same name
I was trying to access one of my embedded bots and got an error about multiple results. I had previously created a bot service and later added another one with the same display name by mistake. The system should have let me pick or at least returned one consistently, but instead it errored out entirely.

Bot services list incomplete after creation
I added a new outgoing webhook bot to my account, but it didn't appear when I checked my list of bots. The bot was clearly saved since I could modify its settings later, but it was missing from the initial listing. I expected all bots associated with my account to show up together.

Bot-stored data disappears after restart
My bot caches its state in local storage, but after a server restart all the cached data is gone. I expected the bot's storage to persist across restarts.

Bot configuration changes silently ignored
When I update a bot's configuration settings through the admin panel, the changes appear to save successfully, but the bot continues operating with its old configuration. I have to restart the bot manually for the new settings to take effect.

Expected: The bot should pick up the updated configuration immediately after saving.

Translation files written to wrong locale folders
When running the message extraction command with multiple locales, the translation content ends up in the wrong language directory — for example, German translations appear inside the French folder. This happens after regenerating locale files and makes it look like translations were lost or overwritten.

I expected each locale's extracted strings to be written to its corresponding folder.

Translation files end up in the wrong language directory
After running the message extraction command, translation JSON files sometimes appear in the wrong language folder—for example, Portuguese translations show up in the Italian directory. It seems to happen inconsistently across runs. Each language's translations should stay in their own matching directory.

Frontend translations end up in wrong locale directories
After running the message extraction command, translation strings appear in the wrong language folders—for example, German translations show up in the French locale directory instead. The locale-to-path pairing gets scrambled between runs.

Plural form detection broken after running message extraction command
After running the translation message extraction command, Django's ability to detect plural forms in templates stops working correctly. Translations that use plural forms no longer display properly until the server is restarted. I expected the command to restore all modifications to Django's template engine before finishing.

Some translation strings are silently skipped during extraction
When I run the message extraction command, a few strings wrapped in translation syntax inside my Handlebars templates aren't being picked up. They're valid translation markers but they don't appear in the generated catalog. I expected every translatable string in the template files to be captured.

Cannot find users by their login email in the provisioning API
When I try to look up a user through the provisioning API using the email they use to log in, the search returns no results even though the user exists. I expected the API to find users by their primary email address, since that's what they use to sign in and receive messages.

Groups returned in strange order
When I fetch groups via the SCIM API they're always returned in the same odd order - not alphabetically by name and not by when they were created. It looks like it's based on some internal database pointer from the parent table. I expected groups to be ordered by their display name so I can reliably paginate through them.

User group search returns no results
When I use the SCIM API to search for user groups by display name, I get back an empty list even though groups with matching names exist in my subdomain. The same kind of search works correctly for individual users.

Adding myself alongside others requires admin permissions
When I try to add myself to a user group along with other members in a single request, the operation fails with a permission error even though I have permission to join the group on my own. Adding just myself works fine, but adding myself plus others requires admin-level permissions.

Adding subgroups silently skips nested groups
When I add multiple subgroups to a parent group at once, some of them don't actually get added. If one of the subgroups I'm adding is already nested under another subgroup in the list, it's silently skipped without any error or warning, even though the API returns success.

Group membership change notifications only reach affected users
When people are added or removed from a user group, only the individuals directly affected receive a notification. Other members of the group never find out that someone joined or left, even though they share the group. I expected all current members to get a message whenever the roster changes.

Group deactivation ignored when editing
When I edit a user group and mark it as deactivated, the API accepts the change without error but the group remains active. Reactivating a deactivated group works fine, but the reverse does nothing. I expected the group to be deactivated after saving the edit.

Removing subgroups occasionally fails with false error
When I attempt to remove a subgroup from a parent group, the request sometimes fails with a message that the subgroup isn't a child of the group, even though it clearly is listed as a direct subgroup. Refreshing and retrying the same operation succeeds.

Realm org type change accepts text input
When I changed the organization type in realm settings, entering a text string didn't trigger an error like other numeric fields do. The invalid value was stored without any warning. I expected the same strict validation that applies to other number-only settings.

Presence check crashes on multi-user updates
When a presence update event contains data for several users at once, the validation crashes with an unhelpful error instead of checking each user's presence individually.

Mixed realm settings updates bypass validation
When sending a realm update with multiple settings in the same event payload, only the first matched setting type is validated while the remaining fields are silently skipped. I expected every field in the update to be checked against its proper schema.

Finished build messages sometimes fail to post
When a build finishes, the webhook message occasionally doesn't appear in the target stream. This happens when the incoming webhook payload doesn't include a results field — the message simply fails silently and no notification is sent. I expected every finished build event to produce a message regardless of whether a results code was provided.

Expected instead: a message should still be posted for finished builds even if the results field is missing, perhaps with a generic status like "unknown".

Build messages disappear when project name is missing from webhook
When a build webhook doesn't include a project name, no message appears in Zulip. This happens intermittently because not all builds report a project name. I expected messages to still post, perhaps using the builder name as the topic instead of crashing silently.

Shared image not displaying in copied message
When I copy a message that contains an image, the image reference appears in my new message but the actual image doesn't show up. The original message displays the image fine, and I can see the image in the original. It's only in my copied message that the image is missing.

Attachment still shown as linked after removing from message
When I edit a message to remove an attached file, the attachment continues to appear as associated with that message in my uploaded files list. The system should recognize the attachment as no longer linked to any message once I remove it from the message content.

Old unclaimed attachments never get cleaned up
I ran the cleanup command to remove unclaimed attachments older than five weeks, but the files are still sitting in storage after multiple runs. The upload space usage shown in the admin dashboard hasn't changed at all, even though many files were uploaded but never attached to any message.

Upload space indicator jumps by more than the attached file size
When I attach a file, the upload space counter in the sidebar increases by much more than the size of the file I just uploaded. It looks like it includes other people's uploads too, so I can't tell how much of the storage I'm actually using. I expected the number to reflect only my personal uploads within the realm.

Setting a field to empty doesn't save
When I explicitly set a custom profile field to empty via the API, my previous value reappears after refreshing the page. I expected the empty value to be saved, but it seems like the system treats an explicit empty value the same as not providing the field at all.

Custom display names lost on invitations
When I send an invitation with a custom display name, the person who accepts it shows up with only their email address as their name. Other invitations from the same account work fine, so it seems like the name field gets dropped somewhere.

Streams I've unsubscribed from still appear in my active subscriptions
After unsubscribing from a stream, it remains visible in my list of active subscriptions even after refreshing the page. The stream's color hasn't changed and I can still see messages from it. I expected the stream to move out of my active subscriptions entirely.

Analytics data still uploading despite setting level to basic
I changed the analytics upload level to "basic" in the server settings, but the server is still sending all usage data to the analytics endpoint. After restarting the server, the same thing happens — only the basic metrics should be sent, not the full dataset.

Edit history shows wrong changes
When I edit only the content of a message without changing anything else, the edit history still shows that the topic was modified. Similarly, when I move a message to a different stream, the "moved" label doesn't appear. I expected the edit metadata to accurately reflect only what I actually changed.

Export still visible after deletion
After I delete a realm export from the admin panel, it continues to appear in my exports list even after refreshing the page. I expected the deleted export to disappear immediately.

Export status notification not received by admins
After deleting a realm export as an administrator, I expected to see a real-time notification in my admin dashboard showing the updated export list. However, no notification appeared and I had to manually refresh the page to see the change reflected.

Duplicate stream groups created when re-running the command
I ran the management command to create a default stream group with a specific name and description. Later, I ran the same command again but with a slightly different description text, and now I have two groups with the same name showing up in the sign-up flow. I expected the command to find and update the existing group rather than creating a duplicate.

No validation when --streams is empty
I ran the command with an empty value for --streams and didn't get an immediate error. The command appeared to succeed but created a group with no usable streams. I expected a clear message requiring at least one stream name.

Event handler status missing after successful plan upgrade
After upgrading my plan, the subscription details page shows the payment as completed but the event handler section is blank. I expected to see the processing status confirming the webhook was handled successfully.

No event details shown for failed payments
When a payment intent is processing or has failed, the event history doesn't appear in the admin view. I expected to see the same tracking information that shows up once a payment succeeds.

Subscription type causes error when viewing account details
Attempting to view my subscription information triggers a server error after an upgrade. The system is unable to translate the stored subscription type into a readable format, which prevents the account details page from loading properly.

Webhook event status display crashes for certain records
When viewing the event handler details in the subscription dashboard, the page crashes with a server error for some webhook events. The issue occurs when the event's internal status doesn't match any of the predefined states. I expected the status to display as "unknown" or similar rather than causing a complete page failure.

Subscription status shows error instead of readable value
When viewing my subscription details, the status field throws an error rather than showing a human-readable label like created or completed. This happens when the subscription record contains a status value that doesn't match the expected options.

Animated emoji shows as a still image
I uploaded a GIF custom emoji through the admin settings, but it appears as a frozen frame in chat instead of animating. The same file plays fine when downloaded from the server. I expected every animated emoji I add to animate automatically.

Generic server error when removing a non-existent emoji
When I try to delete a custom emoji that doesn't exist or was already removed, the request fails with a generic server error instead of a clear message saying the emoji wasn't found.

Unread message count crashes on topics with non-lowercase names
When I have topics whose names contain uppercase letters (like "Feature Request" or "API Help"), the unread message calculation sometimes throws an error and my unread count doesn't update correctly. It works fine for topics typed entirely in lowercase. I expected topic name casing to not matter — the system has always treated topic names case-insensitively elsewhere.

Muted topics still appear in search results
After muting a topic in a stream, messages from that topic still show up when I search within that stream. I expected them to be excluded from search results just like they are from the normal message feed.

Topic visibility changes not taking effect
After changing a topic's visibility setting from muted to followed, the topic still disappears from my home view when there are no new messages. My settings page shows the updated value, but the topic behaves as if it has the default inheritance policy.

Muted topic missing from my muted list
I muted a topic in a stream, but it doesn't appear in my muted topics list. Other topics I've muted are displayed correctly. The mute is definitely saved since I can see it when I revisit the stream settings, but it's missing from the list of muted topics.

Topic visibility settings disappear after stream is deactivated
When I deactivate a stream, all my topic visibility settings for that stream vanish from the system. After reactivating the stream, I find that my explicit topic configurations are gone and I have to set them up again. I expected my topic settings to persist regardless of whether the stream is active or not.

Missed message notification emails never arrive after being away
When I return after several hours of being offline, some of the messages I was directly mentioned in never triggered the expected batched email notifications. The messages still show as unread in the app, but no email ever came through. I expected the system to send out email notifications for all missed messages during the time I was away.

Missed message notification emails aren't batched together
When I send several messages in quick succession to a stream, I receive multiple separate email notifications instead of one consolidated batch. I expected all messages received within my batching window to be combined into a single email.

Email notifications arrive with wildly inconsistent delays

After receiving a message, the email notification sometimes arrives within a second but other times takes nearly ten seconds. I can't figure out what triggers the difference—it seems random. I expected notifications to arrive consistently within a few seconds of receiving the message.

Missed message email notifications take over a minute to arrive after a brief glitch
After a short database hiccup, the worker kept retrying but waited progressively longer between attempts. Even after the database recovered, the retry delays kept compounding, leaving me waiting over a minute for missed message emails.

Application hangs during startup in staging environment
After deploying to our staging instance, the process freezes and never becomes ready. The server appears completely hung with no error output, and health checks fail because the initialization sequence never completes.

Commit links show (None) in notifications
When a commit from our Beanstalk integration doesn't include a web link, the resulting notification displays the commit reference with a broken link showing (None) instead of simply omitting the link. We expected the commit to still appear, just without a clickable URL.

Empty branch filter silently stops all Git push notifications
When configuring the Beanstalk webhook, entering an empty value in the branches-to-notify field causes every Git push to be silently ignored. No error appears and no notification is sent — it just looks like the webhook has stopped working entirely. I expected either all branches to be notified (treating an empty field as "no filter") or a validation error telling me the input was invalid.

Newly created channels don't appear in the sidebar
After bulk creating channels, they don't show up in the left sidebar or channel list. They're visible in server settings but inaccessible from normal navigation.

New users missing from full members group after bulk import
After running a bulk user creation, some newly created accounts can't access channels that require full member status. These users are only in the basic members group, while manually created accounts have both memberships.

Channels sometimes appear broken after bulk import
After importing a realm, some channels show up in the sidebar but display incorrectly or are missing information. The channels are accessible directly but their internal recipient linkage isn't always established. Reloading the page doesn't fix it.

Import crashes on a single malformed message
When importing from Microsoft Teams, the entire import fails if any message contains HTML that can't be parsed. I expected it to skip that one message and continue with the rest of the data.

Messages silently disappear during Microsoft Teams import
When I import a large Microsoft Teams export into Zulip, many messages are missing from the resulting data. They don't show up as errors or skipped items - they just aren't there at all. This only happens with larger imports containing hundreds of messages across multiple files.

Announcements channel set to archived team
After importing from Microsoft Teams, our archived 'All company' team became the default announcements channel. New users signing up are directed there but can't post because the channel is inactive. The import should skip archived teams when picking the announcements channel.

Import crashes with unhelpful error when a Teams user has no email
Running a Microsoft Teams import fails partway through with a cryptic assertion error that prints the entire user record. The problem is caused by a user account in Teams that has no email address set, but the error message doesn't explain this or tell me how to fix it.

Messages silently dropped during Teams import
After importing my workspace from Microsoft Teams, several conversations are missing messages that I know existed in Teams. The import completes without errors, but the message count doesn't match what I see in Teams. I expected all user messages to be imported.

Extra spaces in settings navigation instructions
When I follow the help instructions to navigate to a bot or user settings page, the rendered text has a large gap between the clickable link and the word "tab". For example it reads something like "Navigate to the Bots tab" with many spaces between the link and "tab", making the instructions look broken.

Settings tab instructions appear on wrong lines in help docs
When my help documentation contains duplicate lines, the settings navigation instructions show up on incorrect lines or get duplicated. Each settings tab directive should only affect its own line.

Settings tab reference crashes help rendering
When I include a settings tab link in my help documentation using an identifier that doesn't match any known setting, the entire help page fails to render with an error. I expected the unrecognized reference to either display as plain text or show a helpful message about available options instead of breaking the whole page.

Settings help links rendered twice
On certain organization settings pages, the step-by-step navigation instructions contain duplicate sentences pointing to the same setting. For example, there are two "Go to" lines instead of one.
